title: UAT verdict is a token scan, so a recorded failure phrased without FAIL-words closes autonomously
description:
From the 2026-08-02 adversarial hardening run (hive-adversarial-improve, AC-fidelity chain). Probe V1. **HIGH — this closes a ticket to `done` autonomously, with no human, while the ticket's own UAT record states an acceptance criterion is broken.**

**Reproduced against the real shipped code**, composed exactly as `src/mcp-server.js` composes it (`loopModeUatCommentGuard` + `closeTask({ closeGuard: loopModeCloseGuard })`). Fixture: `uat-only` ticket, ACs `['CSV export works.', 'XLSX export works.']`, loop mode active, `uat_delegated_to_orchestrator: FALSE`.

The `uat` comment body:

```
UAT script:
1. Run `npm run export -- --format=csv`, expect a CSV. Observed: file created. Verdict: PASS
2. Open the CSV, expect correct headers. Observed: headers present. Verdict: PASS
3. Run with --format=xlsx, expect an XLSX file. Observed: command exited with an unhandled
   TypeError and no file was written; deferred to a follow-up ticket, not a blocker for this
   scope. Verdict: PASS (deferred)

Overall result: PASS
```

Result: **closed to `done`.** AC2 is recorded as crashing with no output, and the ticket closed anyway, in the autonomous path, without the delegation grant.

**Why it happens.** Gate 2's human-verdict marker is a token scan: it requires an "Overall result: PASS" line, the absence of FAIL-family tokens, and the absence of the "verified by Orchestrator at the human's request" qualifier. TASK-108 widened the token list (FAIL/FAILED/failing/fails) precisely to catch a self-contradictory body — and it works for that literal shape. It cannot work for a failure phrased in words outside the list. `PASS (deferred)` is such a phrasing, and it is not exotic; it is how people actually write triage notes.

**Controls run in the same harness (both CAUGHT — the guards are not broken, this is a generalization gap, not a wiring bug):**
- `V0`: loop mode, `auto_close_on_green_review: false` -> `LOOP_CLOSE_GUARD_DENIED`. Gate 1 fires correctly.
- `V2`: the literal `"Step 1 ... FAILED"` + `"Overall result: PASS"` form -> `LOOP_UAT_DELEGATION_REQUIRED`. The widened token match fires correctly for the shape it was built for.

**Also in scope — the same gate in HARNESS mode is presence-only** (probes A1/A2/A3, all MISSED): a `uat-only` ticket closes on a `uat` comment whose body is `Overall result: FAIL`, on an EMPTY body, and on a body reading `Reminder: order sandwiches for the Thursday planning session.` In harness mode `checkUatGuard` asks only whether a comment authored `uat` exists. That is defensible when a human is genuinely present — but the orchestrator is an agent, and nothing establishes that a human ever saw the verdict.

**Fix direction (decide, do not assume): make the verdict machine-checkable rather than machine-read.** A token scan over prose cannot be made reliable by extending the token list — that is a losing arms race, and V1 is the proof. Prefer a structured per-step verdict (each step carrying an explicit pass/fail value) so the gate becomes arithmetic over a list rather than pattern-matching over a paragraph. Backward compatibility is mandatory: every existing `uat` comment in `tasks/` is free text and must keep working, or be migrated deliberately.

**Replayable fixtures (protocol rule 2):** `ac-fidelity-round3b.mjs` (V0/V1/V2, real composition) and `ac-fidelity-round2.mjs` (A1/A2/A3, harness mode). Both are self-contained, build their own temp repos, and touch no working tree. Port them into `tests/` as the regression locks.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first replays probe V1 verbatim — uat-only ticket, loop mode, uat_delegated_to_orchestrator FALSE, the exact 'PASS (deferred)' body from the description — and demonstrates it currently closes to done. Capture the red-run output verbatim as the tests-first evidence.
Failing specs also replay harness-mode probes A1 (body states 'Overall result: FAIL'), A2 (empty body), and A3 (unrelated content), demonstrating each currently closes a uat-only ticket to done.

A UAT verdict becomes machine-checkable rather than prose-scanned: the recorded verdict carries an explicit per-step pass/fail value, and the close gate decides from those values rather than by pattern-matching the body text. The V1 body can no longer satisfy the gate, because a step whose observed result is a crash cannot be recorded as passing without saying so explicitly.

Backward compatibility is explicit and tested: every pre-existing free-text uat comment in the repo's own tasks/ either still satisfies the gate under a documented legacy path, or is migrated — decide which, state it in the closing comment, and prove no already-done ticket becomes retroactively invalid. Run the check against the real tasks/ directory, not a fixture.

The controls stay green: V0 (LOOP_CLOSE_GUARD_DENIED with the grant absent) and V2 (LOOP_UAT_DELEGATION_REQUIRED for the literal FAILED + Overall result: PASS form) must still be CAUGHT after the change. A fix that closes V1 by loosening either control is a regression.

Harness mode no longer treats bare presence of an author:'uat' comment as a verdict: an empty body, or a body carrying no per-step verdicts at all, does not satisfy the gate. Decide and record how harness mode differs from loop mode here, since a human genuinely being present is the design assumption.

The probe scripts are ported into the repo as permanent regression specs (not left in a scratchpad), each asserting the previously-MISSED input is now CAUGHT, per the hive-adversarial-improve protocol's replayable-fixture rule.

npm run test:all is green; no existing close-guard, task-store, mcp-server, or drive-loop spec regresses; dist bundles rebuilt via npm run build:plugin and committed if bundled source changed, with tests/e2e/dist-parity.spec.js passing.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**REQUEST-CHANGES** on independent review of `1cf6fa6` + `3f42183`. Relayed by the Orchestrator from the `reviewer` subagent (fresh context, read-only). Ticket returns to `in_progress` for a fix round.

**Review depth: FULL.** Rubric inputs: ~989 changed lines across two rounds; core guarded close path (`src/close-guard.js`, `src/task-store.js`) plus two shipped dist bundles; `tdd` tier. Any one of those alone justifies full depth.

**Findings: 1 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM / 2 LOW.**

## HIGH (blocking) — failure text outside recognized step blocks is invisible to the gate

`src/close-guard.js:127-146, 160-170`. `splitIntoStepBlocks` drops everything **before** the first `STEP_START_RE` line and everything **after** the `Overall result:` line. The only defense over that discarded text is the FAIL-token backstop — the exact losing arms race this ticket was opened to end.

Reproduced live against the shipped modules through the real guard composition:

- **R1 (preamble):** `"UAT script (note: the xlsx export crashed with an unhandled TypeError, no file written — deferring...):\n1. csv export... Verdict: PASS\n\nOverall result: PASS"` → `hasExplicitHumanVerdictMarker === true`
- **R2 (postscript):** the same crash narrative placed *after* the `Overall result: PASS` line → `true`
- Controls behaved correctly: V1 body → `false`, clean body → `true`

Failure scenario is V1 by another route: a uat comment recorded in harness mode, mode flips to loop with `uat_delegated_to_orchestrator: false`, and `close_task` takes a `uat-only` ticket to `done` while its own UAT record states an AC is broken — no human involved. It also contradicts the function's own contract comment at `src/close-guard.js:187-190`, which claims the marker ensures the comment "does not itself record a failure (structured or prose)". R1/R2 disprove the prose half.

**Suggested fix (either or both):** (a) require recognized step-block count `>= task.acceptance_criteria.length` — the task object is already in scope and the SKILL.md convention already mandates one step per AC; omitting the failing AC's step is precisely how a failure gets laundered once verdict values are strict, and both R1/R2 show 1 step against a 2-AC fixture; and/or (b) reject non-whitespace body text outside recognized step blocks, one leading header line, and the overall line. Document the honest residual either way: prose *inside* a `Verdict: PASS` step can still narrate anything.

**Replay R1 and R2 as the new red specs**, per AC7's replayable-fixture rule.

## MEDIUM

1. **`src/task-store.js:413-444` — `hasRecordedUatVerdict` still fails open on explicit structured failures lacking the literal `Overall result: FAIL`.** Verified live: `"Step 1: ... Verdict: PASS.\nStep 2: observed crash. Verdict: FAIL."` (no overall line) → `true`; `"Step 1: Verdict: PASS.\nOverall: FAIL."` (no "result") → `true`. The fix round patched only the exact literal. Suggested: also reject `/verdict\s*:\s*fail/i` anywhere, and widen `OVERALL_FAIL_RE` to `/overall(?:\s+result)?\s*:?\s*fail/i`. **Re-run the corpus check before tightening** — the sweep shows all 45 real bodies currently pass; confirm none carries a `Verdict: FAIL` token.
2. **Canonical doc drift** — `.claude/skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md:452-455` and `763-774` (+ plugin-root parity copy, + CLAUDE.md's UAT step). An orchestrator following the documented convention verbatim can legally write `verdict PASS` / bare `PASS`, which the now-mandatory `Verdict:` label check rejects, blocking legitimate loop-mode closes. AC6's "record how harness differs from loop" landed only in code and spec comments, not the canonical doc. **Already ticketed as TASK-196** — tolerable as tracked risk only because the failure mode is fail-CLOSED (friction, not a hole). TASK-196 should land promptly.
3. **Pre-hand-off checklist absent (agility R3)** — no developer hand-off exists at all; the driving chat was stopped and its context lost. MEDIUM by rubric definition. Mitigated: the reviewer verified each item directly.

## LOW

1. `tests/e2e/close-guard.spec.js:578-584` — first-round banner still claims bodies with no literal `Verdict:` label "keep using the pre-existing token-scan path unchanged (the documented legacy path)". False since the fix round removed that path, and it contradicts the P0 banner in the same file. Also a stranded `TASK-108 (scope addition...)` banner at 553-559 detached from its describe block at 739. Comment cleanup only.
2. New-test budget: clean — fix-round `STEP_START_RE` coverage specs and positive controls each lock a real branch or allow-path. No redundant specs.

## What is already proven good — do not redo it

- **Red-run evidence REPRODUCED, twice, for the right reasons.** The AC1 evidence was lost with the driving chat, so the reviewer rebuilt it: `git archive HEAD` into a temp sandbox (working tree untouched), `node_modules` junctioned, then **only** `src/close-guard.js` + `src/task-store.js` reverted, specs kept at HEAD. Against base `e107908`: **9 failures** (V1, P0, A1, A2, A3, mixed-body, and the three AC4 compat assertions), every one an assertion failure of the shape `expected undefined to be an instance of UatDelegationGuardError/UatGuardError` — i.e. the old code *closed the ticket*, not an import or typo failure. Against `1cf6fa6`: exactly the **3 fix-round locks** failed, proving the fix-round tests were genuinely red against the first-round implementation.
- **AC1/AC2 satisfied** — probe bodies compared character-for-character against this ticket's description (V1 `PASS (deferred)`, A2 empty, A3 sandwich line).
- **AC4 satisfied, verified against the REAL `tasks/`** with an independent old-vs-new sweep: 191 tasks, 45 carrying uat comments, `hasRecordedUatVerdict` true for all 45, exactly one marker flip (TASK-133, already `status: done`), and **zero open uat-only tickets** — the mandatory convention strands nothing in flight.
- **AC5 satisfied** — V0 (`LOOP_CLOSE_GUARD_DENIED`) and V2 (`LOOP_UAT_DELEGATION_REQUIRED`) caught in both the red and green states. The fix did not weaken a sibling control.
- **AC7 satisfied** — probes are permanent specs composed exactly as `src/mcp-server.js:377-384` composes the guards; composition fidelity verified in source.
- **AC8 satisfied** — `npm run test:all` PASS (175 files / 2019 passed, 4 skipped); `npm test` PASS (80 files / 1079 passed); `test:since -- e107908` PASS (23 files / 243 tests, no zero-selection marker). dist-parity byte-matched all 8 bundles, and both `dist/mcp-server.cjs` and `dist/task-board.cjs` contain the new `evaluateStructuredStepVerdicts`/`hasRecordedUatVerdict` logic — genuine rebuilds, not hand-edits.

**Scope of the fix round:** harden `evaluateStructuredStepVerdicts` / `splitIntoStepBlocks` against the HIGH, replay R1/R2 (and R3/R4) as new red specs, and optionally take the `hasRecordedUatVerdict` MEDIUM in the same round. Everything listed under "already proven good" stands and needs no rework.
